title: Carry structured metadata through Human primitives
description:
As a procedure author, I want human interactions to carry generic resource and response contracts, so that a host can present and validate durable actions without runtime-specific patches.

Feature: Structured human interaction metadata

Scenario: Preserve optional action context
  Given a Human interaction has an action key, resource references, preconditions, expiry, response schema, and UI hints
  When Tactus emits the interaction through a host adapter
  Then every field is preserved unchanged
  And opaque values are not reconstructed

Scenario: Validate a structured review response
  Given a review declares a JSON response schema
  When the host returns a response
  Then a conforming response resumes the procedure
  And a nonconforming response fails without advancing
  And replay returns the same accepted response

Scenario: Preserve compatibility
  Given an existing procedure uses Human approve, input, review, notify, or escalate without structured metadata
  When it executes
  Then its observable behavior remains unchanged

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Validation update: full isolated Tactus suite passed with 4,203 tests; 449 Behave scenarios and 24 stdlib tests also passed. After formatting the one new runtime test, Black and Ruff pass across the repository and the 153 focused structured-HITL/runtime tests pass.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Model-backed sandbox acceptance exercised this worktree through a persisted structured review, child response, atomic parent claim, and procedure replay with no operational mutation. Plexus currently resolves released Tactus 0.51.5, which lacks these new runtime capabilities; Tactus must be released before the Plexus workflow can be deployed without a local source override.
